chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ibn Ri'ab, from Zurays al-Kunasi, from Abu Ja'far (عليه السلام), who said:

Humran said to him: “May I be sacrificed for you, what is your view regarding what occurred in the matter of 'Ali, al-Hasan, and al-Husayn (عليهم السلام), and their rising and their standing for the religion of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and what befell them from the tyrants killing them and prevailing over them, until they were killed and overcome?”

So Abu Ja'far (عليه السلام) said: “O Humran, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, had indeed measured that for them, decreed it, carried it through, made it binding, then brought it to pass. So it was through prior knowledge of that, conveyed to them from the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, that 'Ali, al-Hasan, and al-Husayn stood forth; and it is with knowledge that whoever among us remained silent remained silent.”

key_terms.الطَّوَاغِيتِ: the tyrannical usurpers or rebellious oppressive powers
key_terms.بِتَقَدُّمِ عِلْمِ: through prior knowledge already conveyed beforehand
key_terms.خُرُوجِهِمْ: their rising forth or going out in public action
key_terms.صَمَتَ: remained silent or refrained from outward action
key_terms.قَدَّرَ: measured and determined by divine decree
key_terms.قِيَامِهِمْ: their standing up to uphold the religion of Allah

ai.seo_question: How does al-Kafi explain the uprising and suffering of Imam 'Ali, Imam al-Hasan, and Imam al-Husayn (عليهم السلام)?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that the sufferings and stand of Imam 'Ali, Imam al-Hasan, and Imam al-Husayn (عليهم السلام) took place according to Allah’s decree and prior determination. It also states that their actions, as well as the silence of other Imams, were based on divinely informed knowledge received from the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم. The narration highlights divine decree, the Imam’s knowledge, and principled action in the face of oppression.
